source.title: Learning from Training Dynamics: Identifying Mislabeled Data Beyond Manually Designed Features
source.authors: Qi Jia; Xu-Hong Li; Lei Yu; Jiang Bian; Peng-Hao Zhao; Shu-Peng Li; Haoyi Xiong; D. Dou

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied; no apparent truncation or garbling affecting the relevant result.
record.tranche_reason: Reports whether models fit partially corrupted training labels, a related test of fitting noisy labels, but does not test completely random labels or report training error directly.
record.gate_note: The relevant result is the authors' explicit statement that most models can fit noisy samples. Detection scores, test accuracies after removing suspected mislabels, and cited findings do not measure the claim versions and are not rows.
record.test_reason: Although primarily a mislabel-detection study, its own clean-versus-noisy training dynamics bear on V6, and its unfiltered-training baselines across noise ratios bear on V4. It does not test V1's completely random labeling.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the Appendix B.1 acquisition statement, but misses the main conclusion: an LSTM trained on synthesized-noise training dynamics detects mislabels across datasets without further adaptation, and dataset cleaning complements robust-learning algorithms. The authors do not conclude that completely random labels were fitted to zero training error.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains classifiers on datasets with varying synthesized label noise to obtain training dynamics; it does not use complete random labeling as the claim specifies.
record.method_sensitivity: The study varies noise ratios and noise distributions, but does not report how those settings change training fit.

fits_no_version.finding: The LSTM detects mislabeled samples across datasets, and filtering or correcting suspected mislabels improves downstream test accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training dynamics can identify label errors and support dataset cleaning.

fits_no_version.finding: LIME assigns greater detector importance to the first half of training.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Early training dynamics are useful features for mislabel detection; detector feature importance does not establish when noisy labels are memorized.

record.problems: The fit result is a broad statement about “most models”; no model-specific results, training-error values, or test errors are provided for it. The text does not establish fitting under complete random labeling.
record.rows_left_out: Detection metrics, retraining accuracies after removing suspected mislabeled samples, and data-debugging comparisons concern label identification or downstream accuracy, not the claim versions' model-fitting outcomes.

untested.parts: Completely random labeling, zero or near-zero training error, chance test performance, and unchanged architecture and hyperparameters relative to true-label training.
Relative time to fit true and random labels, and convergence slowdown as corruption increases.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect training fit at each noise ratio and the complete trajectory from no corruption to entirely random labels.
Comparisons establishing whether explicit regularization prevents memorization or is necessary for generalization.

A direct demonstration that shared real-data patterns are learned before noisy labels are memorized; the supplied figure text establishes different dynamics and fitting difficulty but does not specify memorization onset.

missing.what: Standard, unfiltered-training test accuracies across symmetric noise ratios, separately for CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100. These baselines bear on V4 independently of the detector comparisons.
The study's own comparison of clean and noisy samples' given-label probability trajectories, including lower means and higher variance for noisy samples and the stated greater fitting difficulty.
missing.locator: Figure 1 and caption; Section 3 opening paragraph

record.verdict_notes: Verdicts on missing results use the supplied text. Detection scores and detector robustness do not measure memorization. No verdict treats an untested component as a scope limitation.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test completely random labeling of the entire training set or report test error at chance; the fit statement concerns noisy datasets with varied corruption ratios and does not give a numerical training error.

rows.subject: Most models
rows.operation_detail: Trained models on datasets with noisy labels while recording training dynamics.

conditions.value: synthesized symmetric and asymmetric noise at different ratios
200 epochs; SGD or a variant; other hyperparameters as described in Appendix B.1

rows.measure: Ability to fit noisy training samples
rows.value: Most models can generally fit the noisy samples on the dataset ideally within the desired number of rounds.
rows.locator: Appendix B.1, Models and Acquisition of Training Dynamics
rows.note: Aggregate statement; no per-model training errors, exact noise ratios, or numerical fit measure are given.
rows.check: The qualitative claim that most models fit noisy samples sufficiently for collecting training dynamics does not establish zero or near-zero training error. Partial label corruption does not test V1's completely random labeling. This is an acquisition-method statement, not a quantified fitting result.

relationships.condition: Unfiltered standard ResNet-32 training on CIFAR-10/100 with 20%, 40%, 60%, and 80% symmetric label noise; test-performance component.
relationships.reason: Missing from the rows: Table 1 reports monotonically falling standard-training test accuracy, 75.0→56.7→36.7→16.6% on CIFAR-10 and 49.6→37.5→23.8→8.2% on CIFAR-100. Perfect training fit is not established.
relationships.display_finding: Test accuracy declined from 75.0% to 56.7%, 36.7%, and 16.6% on CIFAR-10 and from 49.6% to 37.5%, 23.8%, and 8.2% on CIFAR-100.

relationships.condition: Clean versus mislabeled samples in synthesized-noise Caltech-256; different-learning-dynamics component.
relationships.reason: Missing from the rows: Figure 1 and Section 3 report lower given-label probabilities and higher variance for noisy samples, interpreted as greater fitting difficulty. This supports different learning dynamics without establishing the full temporal ordering.
relationships.display_finding: Noisy samples had lower assigned-label probabilities and higher variance, indicating greater fitting difficulty without establishing the full learning order.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Training on datasets with synthesized label noise
reader_labels.reason: The authors state that most models can fit noisy training samples; R1 supports fitting under these tested noisy-label conditions, with no numerical training-error result.
